title: Catalan Numbers: closed forms for the central-binomial neighbours C(2n,n±1) = n·catalan n
description: Closed forms for the binomial coefficients adjacent to the centre of row 2n, sharpening the parent reflection identity. The right neighbour C(2n, n+1) = n·catalan n, the left neighbour C(2n, n-1) = n·catalan n (by row symmetry), and the second neighbour (n+2)·C(2n, n+2) = n(n-1)·catalan n. The parent reflection-form entry proved only the additive split C(2n,n) = catalan n + C(2n,n+1) and used (n+1)·C(2n,n+1) = n·C(2n,n) as an internal step, but never recorded the resulting closed form of the neighbour itself; this entry solves for it. The closed form makes the strict gap C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n) transparent and recovers the parent's additive split as the one-line consequence C(2n,n) = catalan n + n·catalan n = (n+1)·catalan n. Fully verified over ℕ, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The Catalan numbers Cₙ = (1/(n+1))·C(2n,n) — named for Eugène Catalan (1838) but already studied by Euler and Ming Antu — count an enormous family of combinatorial objects (Dyck paths, triangulations, binary trees) and sit one step off the centre of Pascal's triangle: the central binomial coefficient C(2n,n) equals (n+1)·Cₙ. The reflection principle for lattice paths expresses Cₙ as a difference of binomial coefficients, C(2n,n) − C(2n,n+1), making the near-central entries of row 2n objects of independent interest. This entry pins down the closed forms of those neighbours, which the standard references leave implicit inside the reflection computation.
overview.problemStatement: Sharpen the parent reflection identity by solving for the binomial coefficients adjacent to the centre of row 2n: prove the right neighbour C(2n, n+1) = n·catalan n, the left neighbour C(2n, n−1) = n·catalan n (by row symmetry), and the second neighbour (n+2)·C(2n, n+2) = n(n−1)·catalan n, and certify the strict gap C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n).
overview.proofStrategy: Mathlib gives the multiplicative bridge succ_mul_catalan_eq_centralBinom: (n+1)·catalan n = centralBinom n = C(2n,n), and the binomial step Nat.choose_succ_right_eq, which at (2n, n) reads (n+1)·C(2n,n+1) = n·C(2n,n) since 2n−n = n. Substituting C(2n,n) = (n+1)·catalan n into the step and cancelling the positive factor n+1 yields the headline closed form C(2n,n+1) = n·catalan n. The left neighbour follows from the row symmetry Nat.choose_symm (C(2n,n−1) = C(2n,n+1)). Iterating Nat.choose_succ_right_eq once more at (2n, n+1) gives the second neighbour (n+2)·C(2n,n+2) = (n−1)·C(2n,n+1) = n(n−1)·catalan n. Strict positivity of catalan n (from centralBinom_pos) certifies the strict gap C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n). Everything is elementary arithmetic over ℕ.
keyInsights: The binomial coefficients flanking the centre of row 2n are exact multiples of the Catalan number: both immediate neighbours equal n·catalan n, so they carry the same arithmetic content as Cₙ scaled by n.

The closed form is extracted by cancellation: Mathlib's neighbour step gives (n+1)·C(2n,n+1) = n·C(2n,n); substituting C(2n,n) = (n+1)·catalan n lets the common factor n+1 cancel, isolating the neighbour — a clean illustration of solving an internal step the parent only used in passing.
Row symmetry C(2n,n−1) = C(2n,n+1) means the left and right neighbours are literally equal, so one closed form serves both flanks for free.

Working multiplicatively over ℕ ((n+2)·C(2n,n+2) = n(n−1)·catalan n rather than dividing) keeps every statement in the natural numbers, avoiding the truncated-subtraction and division pitfalls a literal quotient form would introduce.

Strict positivity of catalan n upgrades the reflection identity from a formal subtraction to a genuine strict descent C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n) with gap exactly catalan n — certifying the parent's difference is non-truncated.

conclusion.summary: The binomial coefficients flanking the centre of row 2n are exact multiples of the Catalan number: both immediate neighbours equal n·catalan n (choose_central_succ, choose_central_pred), and the second neighbour satisfies (n+2)·C(2n,n+2) = n(n−1)·catalan n (choose_central_succ_two). The strict gap C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n) (choose_central_succ_lt) is certified, and the parent's additive reflection split is recovered as a one-line corollary (centralBinom_eq_catalan_add_choose). 161 lines, 8 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: These closed forms are the multiplicative counterpart of the parent's additive reflection identity, and they exhibit the strict descent C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n) whose difference is exactly catalan n. Mathlib records neither the reflection difference nor these neighbour closed forms, so the entry fills a small but genuine gap in its Catalan/central-binomial API — useful wherever near-central binomial ratios appear (ballot problems, lattice-path enumeration, generating-function coefficient bounds).
openQuestions: Give the general k-th neighbour closed form: C(2n, n+k) expressed via catalan n and a falling-factorial ratio, generalizing the first and second neighbours proved here.
Connect the strict gap C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n) to a bijective/injective lattice-path argument rather than the arithmetic cancellation, matching the reflection principle's combinatorial flavour.
Use the neighbour closed forms to derive sharp two-sided bounds on the ratio C(2n,n+1)/C(2n,n) = n/(n+1) and relate them to the central-limit behaviour of the binomial distribution.

sections.title: The Right Neighbour C(2n, n+1) = n·catalan n

sections.title: The Left Neighbour via Row Symmetry

mathlibDependencies.description: (n + 1) * catalan n = Nat.centralBinom n. The multiplicative bridge from Catalan numbers to the central binomial coefficient; supplies C(2n,n) = (n+1)*catalan n, used to cancel n+1 and to substitute for the central coefficient.

n.choose (k+1) * (k+1) = n.choose k * (n - k). At (2n, n) gives the first-neighbour relation (n+1)*C(2n,n+1) = n*C(2n,n); at (2n, n+1) gives the second-neighbour relation (n+2)*C(2n,n+2) = (n-1)*C(2n,n+1).
k ≤ n → n.choose (n - k) = n.choose k. At (2n, n+1) gives the row symmetry C(2n, n-1) = C(2n, n+1), so the left neighbour shares the right neighbour's closed form.
0 < Nat.centralBinom n. Combined with the bridge it forces catalan n > 0, certifying the strict gap C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n).
0 < k → k*a = k*b → a = b. Cancels the positive factor n+1 to extract the closed form C(2n,n+1) = n*catalan n.

Obtained by solving the parent's internal step relation (n+1)·C(2n,n+1) = n·C(2n,n) using C(2n,n) = (n+1)·catalan n and cancelling n+1. Not in Mathlib.
choose_central_pred: the left neighbour C(2n, n-1) = n·catalan n (n ≥ 1), via the row symmetry C(2n,n-1) = C(2n,n+1).
succ_mul_choose_central_succ: the multiplicative form (n+1)·C(2n,n+1) = n·centralBinom n — the neighbour is to the centre as n is to n+1.
choose_central_succ_two: the second neighbour (n+2)·C(2n,n+2) = n(n-1)·catalan n, iterating the binomial step once past the first neighbour. ℕ-clean multiplicative form.
choose_central_succ_lt: the strict gap C(2n,n+1) < C(2n,n), certifying that the parent's reflection subtraction is a genuine (non-truncated) difference of size catalan n > 0.
centralBinom_eq_catalan_add_choose: recovers the parent's additive reflection split C(2n,n) = catalan n + C(2n,n+1) as a one-line consequence of the closed form.
